In the forward direction the carbonyl‑ene forms a five‑membered ring, creates a new C–C bond and converts a ketone into a secondary alcohol. Therefore, the retrosynthetic step breaks the C–O bond of the alcohol and the C–C bond of the newly formed ring, regenerating a ketone and an alkene. The precursor that results from this disconnection is a molecule containing a cyclopentanone bearing a CF₃ group and a pendant styrene side‑chain that is allylic to the carbonyl. This precursor can undergo an intramolecular carbonyl‑ene reaction (Lewis‑acid catalyzed) to give the target product in one step.
